verses.text: Now listen, Jacob, my servant. Israel, you're the one I chose.
The LORD made you and shaped you from the womb. He's the one who'll help you, and he says, “Don't be afraid, Jacob, my servant. Don't be afraid, Jeshurun, the one I chose.
I'll pour water on thirsty people and streams on dry ground. I'll pour my Spirit on your descendants and my blessing on your children.
They'll spring up among the grass like willows growing by the streams.
One will say, ‘I belong to the LORD.’ Another will take Jacob's name. Another will write ‘Belonging to the LORD’ on his hand and honor the name of Israel.”
The LORD, Israel's King and Redeemer, the LORD of Armies, says, “I'm the first and I'm the last. There's no God besides me.
Who's like me? Who can call out and announce what happened and lay it out for me, going back to when I established the people long ago? Let them say what's coming and what will happen.
Don't be afraid or let fear take over. Didn't I tell you long ago and show you what was coming? You're my witnesses. Is there a God besides me? There isn't. I know no other Rock.”
Everyone who carves an idol is wasting their time. Those things they love won't do them any good. Their own witnesses don't see or understand, and they'll end up ashamed.
Who makes a god or casts an image that can't do a thing?
Look, everyone who backs the maker will end up ashamed. The craftspeople are only human. Let them all get together and stand up. They'll be scared and ashamed together.
A blacksmith takes up his ax and works over the coals. He shapes it with hammers and puts his arm into the work. When he gets hungry his strength goes, and if he doesn't drink water he gets faint.

A carpenter stretches out a line and marks the wood with a pencil. He shapes it with planes and marks it with a compass. He makes it look like a person, with all a person's beauty, to sit inside a house.
He cuts cedars for himself and takes cypress and oak. He lets a tree grow strong for him among the trees in the forest. He plants a cypress, and the rain feeds it.
Then it becomes fuel. He takes some to warm himself, burns some to bake bread, and makes a god to worship. He carves an image and bows down to it.
He burns part of the wood in the fire. Over part of it he roasts meat and eats till he's full. He warms up and says, “Ah, that's warm. Look at that fire.”
Out of the rest he makes a god, his carved image. He bows low, worships it, and prays, “Save me, because you're my god!”
They don't know and they don't stop to think. Their eyes have been shut so they can't see, and their hearts so they can't understand.

Nobody thinks it through or knows enough to say, “I burned part of it, baked bread over its coals, and roasted meat and ate it. Am I really going to make something disgusting out of what's left? Am I going to bow down to a tree trunk?”
He's feeding on ashes. His own fooled heart has led him off course. He can't save himself or even ask, “Aren't I holding a lie in my right hand?”
Remember these things, Jacob and Israel. You're my servant. I shaped you, and you serve me. Israel, I won't forget you.
I've wiped your wrongs away like a thick cloud and your sins like mist. Come back to me. I've bought you back.
Sing, heavens, because the LORD has done it! Shout, depths of the earth! Mountains, forests, and every tree, burst into song! The LORD bought Jacob back and will show his glory in Israel.
The LORD, the one who redeems you and shaped you from the womb, says, “I'm the LORD, the one who makes everything. I stretched the heavens out alone and spread the earth out by myself.
I wreck the signs of liars and make fortune-tellers look crazy. I turn wise people around and make what they know look foolish.
I confirm what my servant says and carry out what my messengers announce. I tell Jerusalem, ‘People will live in you again,’ and Judah's towns, ‘You'll be rebuilt. I'll raise up your ruins.’
I say to the deep, ‘Dry up,’ and, ‘I'll dry up your rivers.’
I say about Cyrus, ‘He's my shepherd. He'll do everything I want.’ I say about Jerusalem, ‘She'll be rebuilt,’ and about the temple, ‘Your foundation will be laid.’”
